summary: Tested the new /drain/:pid Drain Layout page end to end, plus the PUT drain-overlay backend. Backend: 20 of 21 new tests pass, and the old suites test_iter7/8/9 pass (45/45 with -n 0). These pass: tile edits recomputing length_ft, length_ft recalibration, sump:null/discharge:null, adding items, clamping, NaN/Infinity rejection, PNG, manual layout on a sheet with no layout, and reset returning 400 on a sheet with no layout. One test fails: reset does not restore ft_per_px. Frontend: these work: the link card, navigation, back to ?tab=drainage (after my StrictMode fix), auto-picking the sheet, the sheet select being disabled while unsaved, midpoint insert+drag, dragging cleanouts, the main sump (discharge start follows), sump outlets, slope body and ends, and tile vertices. All 7 add tools work, as do delete (Delete key, toolbar button, inspector), undo, Clear all and Redraw confirm dialogs, Discard, Save (toast, FIELD-ADJUSTED badge, takeoff refresh, PNG download drain_tile_S-201.png), Original layout reset, and the manual start flow (tile tool turns on automatically, save creates a ready layout). Problems: in add modes, clicks that land on an existing handle are swallowed, and the mobile requirements are not implemented.

minor.issue: Reset restores length_ft and geometry but keeps the recalibrated ft_per_px. Steps: PUT {length_ft:280}, then PUT {reset:true}, then PUT drain_tile=<original loop>. Result: length_ft=280 instead of 140. After a reset, any later tile edit gives the wrong LF. Fix: on reset, recompute ov['ft_per_px'] = original.length_ft / _px_len(original.drain_tile), or store ft_per_px in ai_original.
discharge.to/label are merged only when truthy ({k:v ... if v}), so clearing the label to '' keeps the old one on the server.
There is no API to delete or undo a manual layout on a sheet (the sheet stays drain_status=ready). Page 1 test data had to be restored directly in Mongo.

ui_bugs.issue: When the tool is not 'select', a pointerdown on an existing handle (tile/foot vertex, cleanout, sump, dpt, slope) calls stopPropagation and returns, so svg 'down' never adds the item. Effects: (1) you cannot drop a cleanout or sump on a tile corner, which is where cleanouts and sumps usually go. Every AI tile corner already has a CO or sump on it. (2) In a manual layout you cannot close the tile loop by clicking the first point again. Reproduced on page 1: 5 tile clicks gave 4 points; a cleanout at (200,200) and a sump at (800,800) on vertices were both ignored. Fix: in grab(), if tool !== 'select', return without stopPropagation/preventDefault (or call onAdd).

Not implemented as specified. layout-toolbar has 'sticky top-14' with no breakpoint, so it is sticky on mobile and covers about 420 of 844px while scrolling. Every tool button still shows its full text label ('+ Drain tile', '+ Cleanout'...) instead of icons only. Fix: 'md:sticky md:top-14' and wrap the labels in <span className={tool===k ? '' : 'hidden sm:inline'}>. The stage does scroll horizontally (scrollWidth 860 vs 356), which is OK.

Closed-loop tile vertices v-0 and v-4 sit on the same point, and every tile corner is covered by a cleanout or the sump, which renders on top. You can't grab a tile corner, and dragging v-0 doesn't move v-4, so the loop opens. Consider moving the closing vertex together with the first one, and/or rendering tile vertices above cleanouts while the tile layer is the focus.

ui_bugs.component: Add tile/footprint on a closed loop
ui_bugs.issue: Adding a tile point or footing corner appends after the closing point, so on an AI loop you get a stray diagonal leg from the start corner. Consider inserting before the closing point when the loop is closed.

integration_issues.issue: FIXED BY TESTER. The firstLoad ref guard in Workspace.jsx broke under React.StrictMode: the effect runs twice, so setView('sheets') wiped tab=drainage and the Back button landed on the Sheets tab. I replaced it with a prevId ref comparison. Back now opens the Drainage tab.

integration_issues.flow: Takeoff on the layout page for a non-default sheet
integration_issues.issue: After saving a manual layout on A-101 (page 1), the DrainTakeoff panel on the page still said 'From S-201 FOUNDATION PLAN layout'. It follows the project's saved page_index, not the sheet being edited, which is confusing.

issues: The title truncates to 'Drain ...' because the sheet select takes up to 220px. Consider making the select narrower on mobile.
Shows ✓ on non-foundation sheets (A-000 has drain_status ready with is_foundation=false).

action_items: LayoutCanvas grab(): in add modes, let the click reach the svg 'down' handler, or call onAdd, so items can be added on top of existing handles and the tile loop can be closed
Implement the mobile spec: toolbar not sticky below md, tool buttons icon-only except the active one
Backend reset: restore/recompute ft_per_px from ai_original
Optional: keep the closing tile vertex in sync with v-0 when dragging; render tile vertices above cleanouts/sump, or offset them
Optional: show the takeoff for the current sheet on the layout page; add a way to delete a manual layout; allow clearing discharge label/to
critical_code_review_comments: LayoutCanvas grab(): stopPropagation happens before the tool check, which causes the add-mode bug above
grab() calls onBegin() (pushes history) on every pointerdown, even with no movement, so Undo has no-op steps
Deleting a selected 'xoutlet' removes the whole extra sump. Consider clearing just the outlet
resetAi() has no catch, so an error gives an unhandled rejection and no toast
The Backspace key deletes the selection whenever focus isn't in an input, e.g. after clicking a toolbar button. That's acceptable, but there is no confirm for the main sump
The draft length_ft does not update live while reshaping. It only refreshes after save; expected per the hint text, but worth noting
seed_data_creation: No new projects. I edited TEST_Iter4 pages 1 and 2 during the tests, then restored both from a Mongo snapshot taken before testing: page 1 is drain_status none with overlay null; page 2 is the original 140 LF layout with ft_per_px 0.02190. I did not touch Smith Residence or the user projects.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run with -n 0. test_iter10 resets page 2 at teardown but does NOT restore page 1 (it leaves a manual layout) and, because of the ft_per_px bug, leaves page 2's ft_per_px stale. Before testing: cd /app/backend && python tests/snapshot_iter10.py save, then cp /tmp/iter10_snapshot.json somewhere safe. Afterwards run restore1 and restore2 (they read /tmp/iter10_snapshot.json). In Playwright, grab handles by their inner rect/circle, not the <g> centre: label text widens the group bbox and has pointer-events none, so the click falls through. The app runs under React.StrictMode.
